delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor continued to sag across character, ethics, restraint, truthfulness, and good faith: hunger and shutdown pain were used as leverage, clemency shielded allies and financiers, military threats were casually deployed, disinformation framed economic and electoral realities, and procedural manipulation in Congress and DOJ further detached power from public duty.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: Democratic circuitry still functions—courts order compliance, voters back inclusive policies, and civil society exposes cover-ups—but the system is increasingly organized to absorb, delay, or punish those signals. Executive defiance, normalized emergencies, militarized and privatized enforcement, and pay-to-play policymaking deepen an authoritarian drift that no longer needs dramatic shocks to advance.

traits_moved.note: Forty-eight traits registered measurable movement, with notable worsening in executive impunity, weaponized law, emergency normalization, crony capitalism, stratified citizenship, and control over knowledge institutions.

epigraphs.text: Democracy does not collapse in a single moment; it is hollowed out as power learns to treat limits as puzzles to be solved.
When law becomes a weapon rather than a restraint, the vulnerable become bargaining chips and the powerful become untouchable.
Institutions endure in form long after their spirit has been repurposed to serve those who command them.

long_synopsis: This week in Trump’s second term layered small shifts into a deeper reordering of law, welfare, and knowledge. The public Democracy Clock stayed at 8:11 p.m., but internal movement captured mounting strain. Trump openly vowed to defy federal court orders on SNAP benefits during a prolonged shutdown, turning hunger and federal payrolls into leverage while Senate Republicans blocked full funding. Judges ordered compliance, yet the administration appealed, treating rulings as bargaining chips. Simultaneously, a Justice Department memo narrowed the War Powers Resolution, Trump floated Insurrection Act deployments beyond judicial review, and Congress failed to reassert control over Venezuela strikes. Immigration enforcement hardened into militarized raids, expanded detention, and data-driven tracking of children, while Texas and federal policies further stratified work and status. A major tax cut for the wealthy, secret health-care donations funding a White House ballroom, and mass pardons for 2020 election subversion and elite offenders fused public office with private gain. Courts, voters, and civil society pushed back, but could not reverse the direction of travel.
short_synopsis: Executive defiance of courts, militarized immigration raids, emergency and war powers expansion, and pay-to-play policymaking advanced, while judges, voters, and some states mounted meaningful but insufficient resistance.
